summary: Tashi Tsering is a scholar in Tibetology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the Central School for Tibetans and under numerous teachers, later serving at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (~1979–1992) and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.
Tat'yana Katenina was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University from circa 1944 to 1949 and served there as a docent in 1948.

Tatiana Oranskaia is an Indologist and linguist. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1968–1974) and Kendriya Hindi Sansthan (1988), later holding posts at Saint Petersburg State University (1973–1998) and the University of Hamburg (1995–1996; 1998–2016).

Tatsugen Sato was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He earned his doctorate from Komazawa University by 1978, where he served as an associate professor (~1963–1995) and professor (~1977–1995), while also lecturing at Ryukoku and Tokai universities.
Tatsuo Hayashi was a philosopher who studied at Kyoto University from circa 1919 to 1922. He held posts at Toyo University (~1928–1944) as well as Tsuda, Meiji, Rikkyo, and Hosei universities.

Tatsuo Nishida worked in linguistics, Sinology, and Tibetology. He completed his studies and doctorate at Kyoto University (1948–1962), where he served as professor and dean, later holding roles at the National Center for Science Information Systems and Toyo Bunko.

Tavivat Puntarigvivat works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and under Luangpor Teean Jittasubho (1980), later serving at Mahidol University, Kyoto University, and the World Buddhist University.
Taw Sein Ko was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Rangoon (~1881–1883), the Inner Temple (~1892–1893), and the Inns of Court (~1892–1893).

Tawni Tidwell is a Tibetology scholar who received her Ph.D. from Emory University in 2017. She has held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (2018–2019), the University of Vienna (2019), and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (2019).

Teizo Iyanaga was a historian and Japanologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1935–1938). He held academic posts at Nagoya University (~1949–1968), the University of Tokyo (~1968–1976), and Sophia University (~1976–1983).
Tej Ram Sharma is an Indologist and historian. He completed his doctoral studies at Banaras Hindu University (~1965–1968) and held a post at Himachal Pradesh University (attested 1978).
Tendzin Chökyi Gyatso studied under Lobsang Gyatso and the 14th Dalai Lama, and also taught Lobsang Gyatso.

Tenga Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Benchen Monastery, founded Benchen Monastery in 1976, and served as Dorje Lopön at Rumtek Monastery from circa 1967 to 1980.

Tensei Kitabatake was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1950–1955). He served there in multiple roles including professor and president (1995–1999), and later was president of Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University (1999–2005).
Tenshin Tanouye was a Buddhist studies practitioner and scholar who studied under Sogen Omori. He succeeded Omori and founded Chozen-ji.

Tenzin Dorjee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Geshe Lobsang Tsephel, Geshe Sonam Rinchen, and Geshe Dawa, and served at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and Pullahari Monastery (attested 2000).

Tenzin Namdak is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Shes rab bstan 'dzin rgyal mtshan, sGangs ru Tshul khrims rgyal mtshan, and at Menri Monastery (1950–1953), and founded Triten Norbutse Monastery in 1986.

Tenzin Namgha specializes in Tibetology and completed a Ph.D. at Christ University (2010–2016). He held posts at the Dalai Lama Institute for Higher Education (2019–2021), Central Tibetan Administration (2021), and York University (2026).
Tenzin Norbu works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He has held academic posts at Columbia University and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).
Tenzin Tsenyi is a researcher in Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Warsaw (attested 2026) and served there as an assistant-academic teacher from 2024 to 2025.
